name: Alum Cave Trail to Mount LeConte
region: Great Smoky Mountains National Park, Tennessee
why: Through a tunnel in Arch Rock and under the overhang of Alum Cave Bluffs to LeConte Lodge, the only place to sleep on a summit in the Smokies.
book: Parking tag required in the park (any vehicle stopping over 15 minutes). LeConte Lodge cabins by lottery a year ahead. Alum Cave trailhead parking fills by 8:00.
water: Streams low on the trail; drinking water and lunch at LeConte Lodge in season.
dangers: Narrow ledges with cables above the bluffs, icy in winter.
Fog and storms on the summit in summer afternoons.

points.name: Alum Cave trailhead
points.note: On Newfound Gap Road, 14 km from Sugarlands.

points.name: Arch Rock
points.note: Stone steps through a natural tunnel in the rock.

points.name: Alum Cave Bluffs
points.note: A long overhang of dark rock, the turnaround for a short walk.

points.name: Mount LeConte
points.note: LeConte Lodge and Cliff Tops at 2,010 m, the third-highest peak of the Smokies.
